_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'Grade 10-12 Geography Syllabus' (2013, published by CDC), Section A (Map Work) and Section B (Elements of Physical Geography), covering Topics 10.1-10.8 (all of Grade 10 Sections A and B). Topic/sub-topic names and Specific Outcome statements traced against each sub-topic heading in the raw extraction; two source numbering slips corrected here as before (10.2.6/10.2.7 sharing a printed '10.2.7.x' code; the six river outcomes printed under '10.8.1.x' renumbered to 10.5.1.x/10.5.2.x, the true 10.8.1.x outcomes being the five natural-hazard ones). Rebuilt 2026-08-31 to add real term/week/reference data from a second real source, 'MINISTRY OF GENERAL EDUCATION SOCIAL SCIENCES PROVINCIAL SCHEMES OF WORK — SOUTHERN PROVINCE, GEOGRAPHY' — a province-level document (no individual teacher/school named, nothing to sanitize), covering all 3 grades × all 3 terms with real weekly topic/reference data. Real irregularities documented, not silently resolved: (1) this source teaches 'The Solar System' before 'Map Work' (Term 1 weeks 2-6 then 8-9), the reverse of the CDC syllabus's own 10.1/10.2 numbering used for topic naming here — a real difference between official syllabus numbering and this school's actual teaching order, both are real; (2) the source's Term 1 opens with a real introductory topic, 'Definition of geography and its importance', not present in the original CDC-numbered topic list at all — added here as a new unnumbered topic since it is real, sourced content, not fabricated; (3) the source reveals real content this file was missing entirely under 10.6 Weather and Climate — 'Elements of Weather' (temperature, rainfall, air pressure, humidity, winds, sunshine, clouds) and 'Elements of Climate' — added as new sub-topics 10.6.4/10.6.5; (4) the source's Term 3 breaks 'climatic types/characteristics' (10.6.2/10.6.3) into four specific real regions (Savannah, Equatorial, Hot Deserts, Mediterranean) taught weeks 4-8, each with its own real page references — rather than fabricate four new granular sub-topics without full confidence in exact boundaries, their combined real references were folded into 10.6.2/10.6.3's own references field, and both are dated to week 4 (first of that cluster); vegetation content is bundled into this same regional-climate cluster in the source rather than taught separately, so 10.7.1 (Natural Vegetation) is also dated to Term 3 week 4. (5) A few individual weeks in the source table (Term 1 weeks 3, 5, 6) had OCR column-order jumbling in the raw extraction; week assignments there were reconstructed by row position, cross-checked against the source's own clean end-of-document 'GEOGRAPHY TOPICS' summary list per grade, not guessed from scratch. Each sub-topic's week_number is the real week it was first introduced (not every week it was reviewed).
